theoryContent:
Thermal expansion originates from the asymmetric potential well of interatomic bonds:
1. Linear Expansion: as thermal vibration amplitude grows, mean interatomic distance expands following ΔL = α L0 ΔT.
2. Bimetallic Strip: bonding two metals with differing expansion coefficients (like brass and invar) forces the strip to curl towards the lower expansion metal upon heating, forming the basis of mechanical thermostats and circuit breakers.
3. Water Anomaly: unlike typical liquids which contract continuously upon cooling, water exhibits a density maximum at 3.98°C. Between 4°C and 0°C, expanding hydrogen-bonded open clusters cause volume expansion, protecting aquatic life in freezing lakes.
step1Desc: Test equal lengths of copper and invar under identical 100°C heating; note the remarkable dimensional stability of invar.
step2Desc: Switch to bimetallic mode; raise temperature and observe how differential expansion curves the strip and opens the circuit.
step3Desc: In water anomaly mode, cool the water from 10°C to 0°C; observe the meniscus hitting its absolute minimum at 4°C and rising below 4°C.
step4Desc: Enable real mode and inspect the immense internal compressive stress developed if metal ends are rigidly fixed.
